captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a subtraction template used to cut mounting holes for a NEMA stepper motor into a plate. It features a central, elongated oval pilot boss with an inner shaft slot, surrounded by four outer mounting bolt slots. The outer slots include wider, hexagonal nut-retaining chambers at the top, allowing standard nuts to be recessed. All circular and cylindrical features are elongated along one axis to provide adjustment range for sliding the motor.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD script to generate a subtraction template for a NEMA stepper motor mount. The script should support standard NEMA sizes (8, 11, 14, 17, 23, 34, 42) and include adjustable parameters for the plate thickness, shaft clearance diameter, pilot boss diameter, nut size, nut height, and adjustment slide distance.
captions.factory: The code uses a lookup function to map NEMA sizes to standard dimensions for mounting bolts, shaft diameters, and pilot diameters. The main shape is generated by the 'NEMA_Mount' module, which loops from negative to positive adjustment values to translate and duplicate the 'Simple_NEMA_Mount' template, effectively creating elongated slots. Within 'Simple_NEMA_Mount', cylinders represent the bolt holes and shaft holes, while a custom 'nut' module creates hexagonal nut traps by rotating and unioning three intersecting cubes.
